name: Wye Oak
label: Merge
lede: Wye Oak took their name from Maryland's state tree, which a storm had flattened four years earlier. Jenn Wasner's guitar was the band's calling card, and in 2013 she announced she was putting it down.

eras.title: Named for a fallen tree
eras.text: Jenn Wasner and Andy Stack were a Baltimore duo that sounded like more people. Wasner played guitar and sang; Stack drummed with his feet and one hand and played the bass lines with the other. They swapped one name for another, put out a record themselves, and Merge signed them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wye Oak (band) · Wikipedia: Jenn Wasner
years.h: Wasner and Stack form Monarch in Baltimore
years.p: Jenn Wasner on guitar and voice, Andy Stack on drums and keyboards: two people, one band, no bassist.
years.xp: Wasner, born in Baltimore in 1986, sang with her mother from an early age, took classical piano at about five and learned guitar from her mother at twelve.

years.h: Monarch trades its name for a tree that no longer exists
years.p: The duo renames itself after the Wye Oak, the giant white oak that was Maryland's state tree until a storm brought it down in 2002.

years.h: If Children comes out with no label behind it
years.p: Wye Oak's first album is self-released a year before Merge picks it up.

years.cap: Jenn Wasner and Andy Stack on stage, 2008
years.h: Merge signs Wye Oak and reissues If Children
years.p: Merge Records takes on the Baltimore duo and re-releases their debut. Pitchfork reviews the reissue that April.

eras.title: A senior project, then a No. 1
eras.text: The second album doubled as a college assignment. The third made year-end lists and ended up behind zombies on television. Baltimore neighbors Future Islands borrowed Wasner's voice for their own record.

years.h: Stack hands in The Knot as his senior project
years.p: Wye Oak record The Knot at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County, where Andy Stack is a student. It earns him a grade.

years.h: My Neighbor/My Creator fills the gap before Civilian
years.p: The EP bridges The Knot and the album that would break Wye Oak.

years.cap: Wye Oak at Outside Lands, San Francisco, August 2011
years.h: Civilian tops the A.V. Club's best albums of 2011
years.p: Co-produced with [[John Congleton|6da4067f-e6ce-49b6-925c-56e017075038]], Civilian comes out March 8 on Merge in the US and City Slang in Europe.
years.xp:
AllMusic's Tim Sendra heard a record that "sounds brighter and better recorded" than its predecessors, with extra sadness added. Metacritic scored it 81 from 20 reviews; Pitchfork gave it 7.9.

It peaked at No. 137 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on Heatseekers Albums. Stereogum later ranked it No. 95 among the albums of the 2010s.

For the tenth anniversary, on October 22, 2021, Merge reissued it as Civilian + Cut All the Wires 2009–2011, with a second disc of twelve demos and outtakes.

years.h: Wasner sings The Great Fire with Samuel T. Herring
years.p: Baltimore neighbors [[Future Islands|74963434-dcb6-4b14-98cc-99873b06db66]] release On the Water, and Jenn Wasner of Wye Oak duets with Herring on The Great Fire.

years.h: A Walking Dead episode borrows Civilian
years.p: Wye Oak's Civilian scores the Walking Dead episode "18 Miles Out" and turns up in the film Safety Not Guaranteed. Longmire, One Tree Hill and Being Human use it too.

eras.title: Putting down the guitar
eras.text: After years on the road with Civilian, Jenn Wasner stopped playing the instrument everyone knew her for. She moved to bass and synths, started side projects, and Wye Oak came back sounding like a different band.

years.h: Dungeonesse, Wasner's synth-pop side project, gets an album
years.p: Jenn Wasner and Baltimore producer Jon Ehrens release it on Secretly Canadian.

years.h: Wasner sets the guitar aside for the next Wye Oak record
years.p: Spin's headline over the October 30 story says it all: the fourth album is coming without Wasner on guitar.

years.cap: Wasner and Stack at the Belly Up, July 2014
years.h: Shriek hands the guitar's job to synthesizers
years.p: Made at Brooklyn's Rare Book Room with producer Nicolas Vernhes, Shriek comes out April 29 with Jenn Wasner on bass.
years.xp:
Synths now carry the rhythms and the higher melodies the guitar used to. AllMusic's Tim Sendra heard "swooning banks of synths, bleeping key-based melodies, Stack's choppy drum patterns and programs, and Wasner's bouncy basslines."

The singles were The Tower on January 30 and Glory on March 18. Metacritic scored the album 76; the A.V. Club gave it an A-, Pitchfork a 7.2. It peaked at No. 67 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Wye Oak team up with the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra
years.p: Merge announces a Shriek remixes EP and a Wye Oak collaboration with the orchestra.

years.cap: Wye Oak live in Seattle, January 2016
years.h: Tween gathers what didn't fit between 2011 and 2014
years.p: Wye Oak release Tween, songs written, scrapped and repurposed in the years between Civilian and Shriek. The physical edition follows on August 5.

years.cap: Jenn Wasner performing as Flock of Dimes, 2016
years.h: Wasner goes solo as Flock of Dimes
years.p: Jenn Wasner's first solo album, If You See Me, Say Yes, comes out on Partisan Records.

eras.title: Two careers, one band
eras.text: Wye Oak became something the two members came back to rather than lived inside. Jenn Wasner moved to Durham, North Carolina, joined Bon Iver and made solo records on Sub Pop, while the band kept releasing music on Merge.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Louder I Call, the Faster It Runs · Wikipedia: Wye Oak (band)
years.h: A bassist joins the tour for The Louder I Call, the Faster It Runs
years.p: Mixed by [[John Congleton|6da4067f-e6ce-49b6-925c-56e017075038]], the April 6 album has Jenn Wasner and Andy Stack trading nearly every instrument. William Joseph Hackney plays bass on the spring tour.
years.xp: NPR called it the sound of a band shedding uncertainties. Critics heard dream pop over hard beats, and some of Wasner's most orchestral writing.

years.h: Wasner takes a guitar job with Bon Iver
years.p: Jenn Wasner joins [[Bon Iver|437a0e49-c6ae-42f6-a6c1-84f25ed366bc]]'s live band as a guitarist. Covid delays the tour, but she stays, and plays on Bon Iver's 2025 album Sable, Fable.

years.h: Head of Roses puts Flock of Dimes on Sub Pop
years.p: Jenn Wasner's second Flock of Dimes album comes out on Sub Pop.

years.h: Merge compiles Wye Oak on Every Day Like the Last
years.p: The compilation arrives three years after the 2020 No Horizon EP.

years.h: Flock of Dimes' third album is The Life You Save
years.p: Jenn Wasner's third Flock of Dimes record comes out on Sub Pop.
